title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1RE1LD_0LB0LF_1RA1RA_0LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1RE1LD_0LB0LF_1RA1RA_0LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A two-level counter: single 1s at the right end grow by one per round in doubling time while a walker crosses a list of 1-2 words; rebuilt at 2.3e4, 4.05e7 and 1.2e10 steps; open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 182 cells have been visited and 104 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in A on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: No halt in 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps; rebuilds
claims.text: Direct simulation. The fast counter is the run of single 1s (1 0 1 0 … 1) at the right end: it grows by one 1 per round, and each round takes about twice as long as the one before (T′ = 2T + 14 and 2T − 10 alternately in the regular stretches). The slow list was rebuilt at about 2.3·104, 4.05·107 and 1.2·1010 steps (the walker reached the front at step 6.2·109); between rebuilds each round makes one local change in it.

claims.title: Two-level counter
claims.text: Left of it the slow list is a word in a few pieces, written here with /2 for a double 0: mostly 1 2 /2 (that is 1 0 11 00) and 2 1 /2 (11 0 1 00), behind a leading 3 /2. In each round a walker 4 /2 moves one piece to the left, turning the 1 2 /2 it passes into 2 1 /2; when it reaches the leading 3 the list is rebuilt longer and a new walk starts. Not shown for all sizes.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. See the heuristic claims above for what a halt would need.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a two-level counter: a fast counter at the right end of the tape needs twice as long for each round, and each round makes one small change in a slow list of blocks on its left; rarely the slow list is rebuilt. This page runs the machine and shows the rounds.

facts.text: Rounds of the run proved in Lean for any tape further left.
Each round twice as long as the one before.

sections.heading: A fast counter and a slow list
html: Look at the tape each time the head is in state A on the first blank cell right of everything written. The tape is then a word of blocks of 1s and gaps of one or two 0s ((1 2 /2)^4 is four copies of 1 0 11 00, … an unchanged stretch, 1^17 seventeen single 1s). The fast counter is the run of single 1s (1 0 1 0 … 1) at the right end: it grows by one 1 per round, and each round takes about twice as long as the one before (T′ = 2T + 14 and 2T − 10 alternately in the regular stretches).

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine can halt only on its one undefined transition. The regular rounds are proved in Lean for three instances (for every tape further left) and behave the same way in every round seen; a halt could only come from a rebuild of the slow list (seen at about 2.3·104, 4.05·107 and 1.2·1010 steps (the walker reached the front at step 6.2·109)). Rebuilds come after exponentially many rounds, and their rule is not known for all sizes, so the run cannot be followed beyond direct simulation. Since every rebuild seen made the list longer, the machine looks like it runs forever, but that is an extrapolation.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.097).
After 109 steps the tape spans 182 cells (24 left of the start, 155 right), with a density of 1s of 0.571.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:
